title: Folding-wavelet throughput diary (microburst folding experiments)
body:
Quick log — trying a different microburst folding idea: use short 'fold windows' (50ms) to coalesce nearly simultaneous small requests into a single continuous inference stream, but only when wavelet-detected correlation in arrivals is high. Rationale: previous folding attempts (naive time-bucket) worsened tail when noise unrelated; idea is to detect short correlated surges using a cheap wavelet energy detector and engage folding only then.

Hypothesis:
- Folding correlated microbursts will increase GPU utilization by ~6–12% and reduce p99 latency for small requests by ~10–20% without inflating median.
- When arrivals are uncorrelated, detector will keep folding off and avoid increased queueing.

Experiment setup (local cluster vm-3, ephemeral):
- Model: llama2-7b-quant (fp16->8bit sim)
- Runtime: serve-runtime v0.43.1 + folding-proto branch (PR 3124)
- Node: g4dn-like (4xA100-sim in bench harness)
- Concurrency: 64 worker threads, continuous batching enabled
- Folding window: 50ms; wavelet energy threshold sweep: [0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.4] (units: normalized energy)
- Workloads: synthetic small request (avg 12 tokens), mixed small+medium (12 + 48 tokens 70/30), and background steady stream (1 qps per second per client)
- Duration: 12 min per run; 5 warmup min + 7 measurement min
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, gpu-util%, batching efficiency (avg batch size), drop/retry counts, tail amplification factor

Run notes (raw):
- 2025-11-02 10:05: first sweep run. Threshold 0.6: folding engaged too often -> queueing observed, p50 up 5ms, p99 spiked.
- 2025-11-02 10:30: threshold 1.0: calmer. Observed avg batch size increase from 1.7 -> 2.9 during microbursts; tokens/sec +9%; p99 reduced by ~12% on small-only load.
- 2025-11-02 11:10: mixed workload: folding helped median but p95 unchanged; hypothesis: medium requests trigger larger batch formation but also introduce pipeline stalls (KV cache warmup)
- 2025-11-03 09:05: tried 50ms -> 100ms window: marginally higher batching (3.3) but p99 tail increased under low correlation (detector false-positives)
- 2025-11-04 14:20: added a quick cooldown hysteresis (200ms) after folding toggles to avoid rapid on/off thrash. Reduced oscillations in fold state.

Representative numbers (threshold=1.0, 50ms window, small-only load):
- tokens/sec: baseline 18.2k -> folded 19.9k (+9.3%)
- gpu-util: baseline 41% -> folded 47% (+6pp)
- avg batch size: baseline 1.7 -> folded 3.0
- p50 latency: baseline 32ms -> folded 34ms (+2ms)
- p95 latency: baseline 128ms -> folded 115ms (-13ms)
- p99 latency: baseline 380ms -> folded 335ms (-45ms)
- tail amplification factor: baseline 2.1 -> folded 1.7

ASCII sparkline-ish over measurement window (small-only, seconds 0..420):
- baseline p99: |__--__----____-------__________---_____| (high spikes concentrated)
- folded p99 : |__--__--___----___-------_____---___| (shorter deepest spikes)

Observations / gotchas:
- Detector cost is negligible (~0.2% CPU) but needs smoothing; naive threshold causes fold-on for few correlated arrivals then immediate fold-off -> extra queue churn. Hysteresis helped.
- Folding interacts poorly with prefix-preservation caching: when fold aggregates requests with different prefixes, KV cache warmup increases decode time for the second request in folded batch. Need fold-aware cache priming (maybe decode-first-token pass?).
- Mixed-size traffic: medium requests dominate batch token count and mask the benefit for small requests — consider size-aware folding that only folds small requests together and routes medium requests on a separate fast path.
- Retries: small number (~0.04%) of duplicate responses due to race in folding window boundary when client reconnects; track in next run.

Quick conclusions:
- Wavelet detector + fold window can reduce tail for small-request microbursts while improving throughput. Sweetspot around energy threshold 0.9–1.1 and 50ms window with 200ms cooldown.
- Not safe as a global default yet: needs fold-aware cache priming + exclusion for mixed-size critical path requests.

Next experiments (short list):
1) Fold-aware cache priming: prewarm KV for unique prefixes in folded batch. Prototype: 1-token decode for each unique prefix before full batch. Measure added overhead vs tail benefit.
2) Size-aware folding: only fold when all requests in window < 24 tokens. Also test hybrid: fold small together and enqueue medium for immediate dispatch.
3) Probabilistic folding during mixed traffic: allow folding with p=0.5 to test safe partial adoption.
4) Longer runs on dedicated cluster (dedicated infra) to measure day-scale effects and warmup behavior.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to signal fold state to observability (per-request tag) so Console can surface when folding was active? Add header 'x-folded: true' and emit fold_id.
- Does folding increase hallucination risk for function-calling workloads? likely not but needs check.
- Can routing policy be used to steer medium-size requests to alternate pool automatically when folding enabled? Track with routing flag design.

Notes-to-self: push small prototype PR with cache-priming stub; label with SERVE-874 and request infra run next week. Ping @marta for bandwidth. Save these raw logs in gdrive and attach measurement CSVs (local path: /tmp/fold-wave-run-20251102.csv)

End of scratchpad.

-- Kenji
